excluded_functions: None: every function in the three objects is engine (regfree 162 B counted, it is the only way to release the compiled TNFA). Not compiled: regerror.c (37 lines, error-message table), fnmatch.c, glob.c. tre_tnfa_run_backtrack (backreference matcher) is part of regexec's 3452 B even though backrefs are unreachable in ERE mode: it is a static function selected at run time by tnfa->have_backrefs, so the linker cannot drop it.
libc_deps: arm-none-eabi-nm -u over the three Cortex-M4 objects (minus the engine's own __tre_mem_* symbols): calloc, free, malloc, realloc (heap, unavoidable); memcpy, memset, strncmp; qsort (sorting bracket ranges for negation); mbtowc (UTF-8 decoding of pattern AND text, called per character); wctype, iswctype (class assertions [[:alpha:]] etc. - every \w \s \d goes through this), iswalnum (word boundaries), iswlower, iswupper, towlower, towupper (REG_ICASE). No setjmp, no strlen, no stdio, no float. Size of musl's OWN implementations of these on Cortex-M4 (deps_size.txt, same flags): wctype/ctype group 13407 B (iswalpha 3964 + iswpunct 4048 + towctrans 4774 tables dominate), mbtowc + UTF-8 bittab 388, qsort (smoothsort) 946, memcpy/memset/strncmp 896, mallocng malloc/free/realloc/calloc 4575 => 20212 B of libc on top of the 13309 B engine if one links musl itself; an ASCII-only wctype shim (see asciishim.c, ~200 B) could replace the 13.4 KB but changes \w/case semantics.
ram_model: All heap, nothing static: no globals (reentrant), no fixed buffers except 'struct neg' (64 wctype_t = 256 B) in parse_bracket's frame. regcomp: AST nodes, literal arrays, tag/submatch tables and the TNFA are malloc/calloc/realloc'd (tre_mem pool in 1024-B blocks, TRE_MEM_BLOCK_SIZE) plus an explicit parse/traversal stack tre_stack_new(512 entries initial, max 1024000, +128) x 4 B entries; bounded repetitions {n,m} are expanded by COPYING the AST n..m times (tre_expand_ast/tre_copy_ast) so memory grows linearly with the counts. regexec (parallel TNFA simulation, the only matcher used for ERE): per call malloc(num_tags*4) + one calloc block of 2*(num_states+1)*sizeof(reach) + 2*num_states*num_tags*4 + num_tags*4 + num_states*8 bytes, freed on return; no recursion, time O(len*states*tags), so no catastrophic backtracking (0 timeouts in 2088 cases). Measured on the 64-bit host with a counting allocator (heap_out.txt): pattern 'abc' peak 6.9 KB during regcomp / 0.6 KB retained compiled regex; '(a|b)*c{2,5}\\d+' 14.6 KB / 1.8 KB; '(\\w+)\\s+(\\w+)\\s+(\\w+)' 13.6 KB / 2.0 KB; '[a-z]+@[a-z]+\\.[a-z]{2,3}' 9.5 KB / 1.2 KB; 'x{20,40}' 63 KB / 5.1 KB; peak is always inside regcomp, regexec adds < 1 KB. 32-bit ARM structures are about half (tre_tnfa_transition_t 32 B, tre_tnfa_t 68 B, regex_t 32 B on ARM vs 8-byte pointers on host), so expect roughly 3-30 KB peak heap on an MCU. Stack (-fstack-usage, Cortex-M4): parse_bracket 360 B, regcomp 152, regexec 128, tre_add_tags 96, tre_copy_ast 64, others <= 56; recursion only at compile time: tre_ast_to_tnfa (32 B/frame, depth = AST nesting) and tre_match_empty (40 B/frame, depth = catenation chain length), parse_atom recurses once for \\w-style macro expansion.
features_verified: IMPLEMENTED (read in regcomp.c/regexec.c, confirmed with driver probes, ERE mode = REG_EXTENDED): UTF-8 aware matching - pattern and text decoded with mbtowc, '.', brackets, ranges and quantifiers act on code points, offsets are bytes (probes: 'é.' on 'éx' -> 0 3, '[é-ő]+' on 'éíőx' -> 0 6, '(.)(.)' on 'éx' -> groups 0-2, 2-3); '.' = any code point INCLUDING newline unless REG_NEWLINE; '^' and '$' are assertions anywhere in an ERE (anchored to the whole text without REG_NEWLINE; '$' does NOT match before a trailing newline, unlike Python); escapes \\t \\n \\r \\f \\a \\e via tre_macros; \\w \\W \\s \\S \\d \\D expanded to '[[:alnum:]_]' '[^[:alnum:]_]' '[[:space:]]' '[^[:space:]]' '[[:digit:]]' '[^[:digit:]]' (i.e. locale wctype classes, NOT hard-coded ASCII); \\b \\B \\< \\> word assertions (IS_WORD_CHAR = '_' || iswalnum); \\xHH and \\x{HHHH}; any other escaped char is that literal (\\{ \\. \\\\ \\- \\| all work); bracket expressions [..] [^..] with code-point ranges, [:class:] names, ']' first is literal, '-' first/last literal, negation; REG_ICASE via towlower/towupper on literals + bracket ranges (add_icase_literals) and class assertions (Unicode-aware with a Unicode libc, ASCII with an ASCII libc); quantifiers * + ? {n} {n,} {n,m} greedy, RE_DUP_MAX = 255, {0} -> empty, stacked quantifiers (a**, a+?) accepted as nested iterations; alternation '|' including empty alternatives '(|a)' '||'; capturing groups nested arbitrarily, re_nsub counted, submatches via TNFA tags; empty group '()' matches empty and captures (x,x); loops with empty iterations terminate ((a*)*, (|a)+); error codes: REG_BADRPT for leading quantifier or '(?', REG_EPAREN, REG_EBRACK, REG_BADBR, REG_ERANGE, REG_ECTYPE, REG_EESCAPE; backreferences \\1-\\9 exist ONLY in BRE mode (parse_atom: '!ere &&'), the backtracking matcher for them is compiled in but unreachable from ERE. NOT IMPLEMENTED: lazy quantifiers - the AST/TNFA 'minimal' machinery from TRE is still compiled in (tre_add_tags minimal_tags, num_minimals in regexec) but musl's tre_parse always passes minimal=0, so 'x*?' parses as '(x*)?' = greedy (probe 'x*?' on 'xxx' -> 0 3, 'x??' on 'x' -> 0 1); non-capturing groups '(?:...)' (REG_BADRPT); escapes inside brackets ('[\\d]' = backslash or 'd', '[\\]]' and '[\\-x]' break bracket/range parsing -> REG_EBRACK/REG_ERANGE); Perl leftmost-first disambiguation (TNFA parallel matcher = POSIX leftmost-LONGEST + TRE tag ordering: 'a|ab' on 'ab' -> 0 2, '(|a)+' on 'aaa' -> 0 3); Python-style captures of repeated groups ('((a)|b)+' on 'ab': inner group 2 reported unset, Python keeps 0-1); '.' excluding newline needs REG_NEWLINE, which also turns ^/$ into line anchors and removes '\\n' from negated brackets; '\\v' is a literal 'v'; '{,n}' is an error; a '{' that does not form a valid interval is REG_BADBR (Python: literal); no multiline-only flag; no named groups, lookaround, Unicode escapes.

Classification of ALL 675 failures (classify.py, first-matching rule, every failure lands in a bucket, no residue): MISSING FEATURES 622: '(?:...)' 455 (every one of the 455 corpus patterns using it -> compile error REG_BADRPT); lazy quantifiers treated as greedy 126 (462 corpus cases use lazy syntax without '(?:'; 236 of them expect nomatch and most of the rest give the same span greedy, so only 126 differ); backslash escapes inside [...] 41 (\\d \\w \\s \\] \\- inside brackets: 34 give wrong spans/nomatch, 7 are compile errors REG_ERANGE/EBRACK). SEMANTICS DIFFERENCES 53: locale-dependent \\w \\W \\s and case folding (é, ß, ű, 日 count as word chars / fold case under Unicode wctype; Python re.ASCII does not) 23 - these disappear in the ASCII-shim build; POSIX leftmost-longest vs leftmost-first 21 (typically an empty first alternative '|x' or '(|a)+' where Python returns the empty match and musl the longest); POSIX/TRE submatch rules 7 (empty group '()' reported as (x,x) where Python says unset because a later alternative matched, inner capture of a repeated group reset to unset, last-iteration choice differs); '.' matches newline 2. BUGS: 0 attributable (every mismatch is explained by a documented POSIX/TRE rule). TIMEOUTS: 0 (parallel TNFA, no backtracking). The 7 expected-error cases are skipped by the harness; musl rejected all 7 (REG_BADRPT/REG_EPAREN/REG_EBRACK), no hang or crash.
caveats: (1) Size is for the regex engine only; it is not freestanding: it needs malloc/calloc/realloc/free, qsort, mbtowc and the wctype family. Linking musl's own implementations adds 20.2 KB on Cortex-M4 (13.4 KB of it Unicode class/case tables), so the realistic flash footprint of 'musl regex on an MCU' is ~33 KB, or ~20 KB with an ASCII-only wctype shim and a small allocator. (2) Host driver could not use musl's header tree (host libc ABI); hostinc/regex.h is a stub with musl's regex_t layout and the engine links against macOS libc (mbtowc/iswctype from en_US.UTF-8). macOS iswdigit accepts non-ASCII decimal digits ('\\d+' matched Arabic-Indic digits) whereas musl's own iswdigit is ASCII-only - a host artefact that does not affect the corpus (no non-ASCII digits in it, verified by the ASCII-shim run differing only in \\w/\\W/case cases). (3) The lazy-quantifier 'pass' numbers flatter the engine: 462 lazy cases are counted as checked, most pass only because greedy and lazy give the same overall span there. (4) Alternation/leftmost-longest failures are undercounted: the 455 '(?:' cases and 126 lazy cases were classified first and many of them would also hit POSIX-vs-Perl semantics. (5) The engine is POSIX by design: leftmost-longest, no lazy, no (?:), locale classes; making it 'modern basics' compliant would require parser AND matcher changes (the parallel TNFA cannot express leftmost-first priority without the tag-minimize path, which musl removed from the parser but not the matcher). (6) Memory: everything is heap, peak 6-63 KB on the host for ordinary patterns (about half on 32-bit), {n,m} expands the AST by copying; not usable with 'no malloc'. (7) The bminor/musl GitHub mirror in the task text was not found; the official git.musl-libc.org repo at HEAD was used - numbers are identical to a survey run earlier in this session on the same sources ($S/engines/musl/BUILD.txt). (8) Sizes are with measure.sh flags (-Os, function/data sections, no unwind tables); musl's real build uses -Os -ffreestanding -fno-strict-aliasing etc., and glibc/newlib regex would be far larger still.
